root_cause.text: The `lpc18xx_dmamux_reserve` function acquires a reference to the DMA mux platform device (via `of_find_device_by_node` or similar) but fails to release that reference (`put_device`) in all return paths, causing a device reference leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `put_device(&pdev->dev)` before the successful return and creates a common error label `err_put_pdev` that also calls `put_device`, ensuring the reference is dropped on every exit. The error paths that previously returned directly without dropping the reference are now redirected to `err_put_pdev`.

Author: Joachim Eastwood <manabian@gmail.com>
Date:   Sat Jul 11 14:12:06 2015 +0200

    dmaengine: add driver for lpc18xx dmamux
    
    Add support for DMA on NXP LPC18xx/43xx platforms which has
    a multiplexer in front of the PL080 dma request lines.
    
    The mux is a single register in the LPC18xx/43xx CREG block
    and can multiplex up to 4 request lines to each of the 16
    lines on the PL080.
    
    Signed-off-by: Joachim Eastwo
bic_trace_step.reason: In lpc18xx_dmamux_reserve(), the function calls of_find_device_by_node() at line 66 to obtain pdev, which increments the device reference count. However, the function never calls put_device() on any return path: the early error returns (lines 71-73, 76-79, 82-85, 89-92) and the success path (lines 103-112) all return without releasing the reference. This matches the root cause of a device reference leak.
